status: Reviewed: two accepted references, four rejected paintings deleted.
reference_usage: Consulted accepted images for style, materials, faces and individual kit. New scenes are proposals, not automatic canon or additional card selections.
latest_clarifications: Training increases personal magical capacity and efficiency.
Food and rest replenish energy; external magic can also be drawn on or channeled from materials.
Living beings generally convert or channel magical energy more efficiently than machines; this does not cap a large machine's total output.
The Mountain's Lung burns stored mana from stones; the stones are permanently spent afterward.
Portals are rare because of unusual talent and difficult learned technique.
Alignment/emotion/morality relationships remain exploratory; no intelligence or evilness power formula is established.

This is a compelling painting, not a mechanics diagram. A richly lived-in university repair arcade in Ambrel, at clear morning light. The principal subject is an older male artisan-teacher with a long slightly crooked nose, receding grey hair, lean lined face and an ochre wool coat, watching an adult apprentice with short auburn hair and a broad ordinary face. She is repairing a heavy iron window hinge on a low stone workbench: one hand steadies the detached hinge while her other relaxed open hand guides a SINGLE small brass pin hanging a few centimeters above its socket. No visible luminous tether; a tiny glint on the pin and the purposeful alignment make levitation legible. One opened book with indistinct diagram marks lies off to the side, a practical aid rather than magic physically coming out of writing. Hands simply posed and anatomically connected. The teacher points with one hand at the socket without crowding hers. They wear plain well-made cloth, leather apron and rolled cuffs, no ornate wizard uniforms. Through the broad arcade is a glimpse of Ambrel's warm stone university, narrow green waterway, red roofs and a small grounded service crane. Only a couple distant ordinary passersby, no crowd of casters. Main composition is the human triangle of faces and poised pin; background quietly painted. Cream stone, ochre and muted green with small copper highlights. A sense of hard-won skill, intelligence and affection, not a magical school spectacle.

This scene explores the same established idea as the Mountain's Lung, with fresh staging rather than duplicating its exact machine.

A compelling three-quarter-length portrait of a male roadwarden standing on a hillside road just after rain, dark clouds breaking over green fields and a quiet stone bridge. He is a solid practical adult man around forty-five, broad uneven face, pronounced nose, slightly heavy eyelids, short dark hair going grey, close beard and one imperfect eyebrow; appealing through character, not a model. His posture is relaxed but ready, one shoulder angled forward as he looks down the road past us. A slim curved single-edged steel saber with a black curved grip and simple silver S-like guard remains sheathed at his other hip; a small plain field knife sits beside it. Both arms visible and natural: one hand rests on a milestone, the other loosely holds his ordinary gloves. A short dark moss-green shoulder cloak ends around the hip. Afternoon pale gold catches the breastplate edge; the rest is convincing dark painted metal, not mirror chrome. Focal face and beautiful plate forms, less detail in distant farms. Equipment belongs to an individual. No glowing armor, enormous shoulder plates, medals, extra straps or gadget gauntlets.

This is a compelling painting, not a mechanics diagram. An extraordinary high-fantasy painting of a direct fire-working at a ruined mountain aqueduct at blue dusk. Across the broad midground ravine a huge sheet of orange fire curls UP along the jagged stone embankment, like one great wind-caught wave, illuminating ancient arches, slate mountains and a thin silver river far below. This is a rare powerful magical event, not ordinary scenery or a machine. In the near foreground at the left, a small but clearly legible older adult male caster in a plain soot-grey travelling coat braces himself against a broken stone parapet with his LEFT forearm; his RIGHT arm reaches modestly toward the fire, hand open at waist height. Show exactly two arms connected to his torso, both legs planted, a tired hunched shoulder and deeply focused long face, cheeks matte not sweaty. A companion behind him has just reached toward his upper arm in concern. The spell is powerful and his bodily effort matters; avoid an effortless superhero pose. His silhouette is illuminated by the fire with a muted blue sky rim. The person is dwarfed by the curving hot/cool landscape, retaining scale and grandeur like great painted fantasy spell art. No magical weapon, gauntlet, fuel machine, beam from his hand, strings or diagram. The air between hand and distant event remains mostly clear; visual alignment establishes intent without a literal cable. Fine falling embers, grounded stone masses, no gore, exploding bodies or modern destruction. Keep the sweeping composition and fire beautiful, the human drama economical and the background intelligently simplified.

An older female healer with brown skin, broad nose, substantial jaw, silver-streaked short tight curls and an ordinary kind, concentrated face sits beside a tired adult male carter propped on a simple bed. This is a compelling painting, not a mechanics diagram. A haunting but beautiful high-fantasy painting at a disused stone ferry landing beneath a late evening emerald-blue sky. A living adult woman traveller in a simple dark russet cloak sits sideways on a low mooring stone in the near right foreground, ordinary long face in profile, one hand still on her bundled coat. She has turned her head toward a QUIET CONSCIOUS SPIRIT standing a few paces away at the water's edge. The spirit is an older male figure only intermittently present: a listening face and the suggestion of one shoulder and coat collar are discernible in pale grey-blue air, while the lower torso dissolves gradually into the visible reeds and water behind. A faint directed gaze toward the traveller makes the presence feel conscious. Its one partly visible hand remains near its own chest, no detached floating hands. A small warm lantern stands physically on the stone between them, lighting the LIVING woman's sleeve and the landing but not magically powering the spirit. Dark pines, a modest ruined river arch and still water create restrained depth; no flower fantasy or wildlife-painting aesthetic. Muted jade water, deep ultramarine sky, copper reeds and one amber light. Spacious negative areas, strongly designed silhouettes, subtle mystery and sadness with no definite story of resurrection. This is one experimental spirit depiction, not a required appearance for all spirits.
